issue.close_reason: Implemented lib/common.sh inlining during installation. Modified install.sh to inline lib/common.sh content into scripts that source it, making installed copies self-contained. Updated check-installed.sh to ignore expected differences from this transformation. Verified plan-review, spec-review, readme-review, and plan-author all install and run correctly.
issue.description:
Found 2026-08-20 while installing plan-review 2.0. The in-progress lib extraction (uncommitted WIP in plan-author/plan-review/readme-review/spec-review scripts, untracked lib/common.sh) has each script do: source "$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh". Correct inside the repo, but once a skill is installed to ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ that path resolves to ~/.claude/lib/common.sh. install.sh copies only the skill directory, so every refactored script fails at its source line with 'No such file or directory' (verified: installed plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh exits 1). The parent bead's own spec prescribes that exact path, so the defect is in the spec, not just the WIP.

Options: (a) install.sh also installs lib/ to ~/.claude/skills/lib/ — only works if repo skills and installed skills share the same relative layout; (b) guard the source with an inline fallback — defeats most of the dedup; (c) inline lib/common.sh into each script at install time (a tiny build step in install.sh) — repo stays DRY, installed copies stay self-contained. Recommended: (c). Acceptance: plan-review's SELF-TEST fixture and scan-headers.sh run green from the INSTALLED path, and scripts/check-installed.sh reports no drift.

Until fixed, the installed plan-review carries the HEAD (self-contained) scan-headers.sh and score-plan.sh, so check-installed.sh reports drift on those two files by design.
issue.title: install.sh: scripts that source ../../lib/common.sh break once installed (lib/ not copied)

issue.close_reason: Added version field to all 16 SKILL.md frontmatter blocks, created root CHANGELOG.md with skill history entries, and documented versioning convention in README.md Philosophy section. Committed and pushed to origin (d803dca).
issue.description:
Skills are cp'd once and never re-synced (see the drift-checker bead) — there is currently no
signal to a user with an old local copy that a skill has changed upstream. Add a `version:
X.Y.Z` field to every */SKILL.md frontmatter block (start all 14 at 1.0.0) and a root
CHANGELOG.md following Keep a Changelog format, with one entry per skill covering its history
to date (can be reconstructed from `git log --follow <skill>/`).

Going forward, bump a skill's version and add a CHANGELOG.md entry whenever its SKILL.md,
checklists, or scripts change materially (typo fixes excluded). This is a convention change,
not just one commit — note the convention in README.md's Philosophy section.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list); pairs with the drift-checker bead
(jcs-3) which can eventually report version mismatches, not just file diffs.
issue.notes:
Added version: 1.0.0 field to all 16 SKILL.md frontmatter blocks:

- adr, api-design-review, diff-review, gap-review, migration-runbook, plan-author, plan-idea-gen, plan-review, postmortem, readme-review, release-readiness, repo-hygiene, spec-review, test-plan-review, threat-model, usage-statusline

Created root CHANGELOG.md following Keep a Changelog format with one entry per skill covering its history to date (reconstructed from git log --follow <skill>/).

Updated README.md Philosophy section to document the versioning convention: skills should bump version and add CHANGELOG entry whenever SKILL.md, checklists, or scripts change materially (typo fixes excluded).

This supports drift detection - users with local copies can compare against upstream to see if they're missing changes. Pairs with the drift-checker bead (jcs-3) which can eventually report version mismatches.

All changes committed and pushed to origin: d803dca
issue.title: Add version field to SKILL.md frontmatter + root CHANGELOG.md

issue.close_reason: Added scripts/check-installed.sh drift checker that diffs ~/.claude/skills/ against repo copies, with documentation in README.md. Script detects missing, extra, and modified files and exits non-zero on drift. Addresses the same issue that motivated ADR-1 (silent skill copy divergence).
issue.description:
Skills are distributed by `cp -r` into ~/.claude/skills/ (per README.md) with no update or
drift-detection mechanism. Confirmed live on this machine 2026-07-20: the installed
~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh differs from this repo's usage-statusline/scripts/usage-statusline.sh
by one line (installed copy hardcodes `/home/coding` in its commit-scan `find`, repo's current
version generalized to `$HOME`) — silent drift with nobody aware.

Add scripts/check-installed.sh [skill-name...] that, for each named skill (or all skills if
none named), diffs the corresponding directory under ~/.claude/skills/<skill> against this
repo's <skill>/ directory and reports any files that differ or are missing on either side.
Exit non-zero if drift is found. Document usage in README.md under a new "Checking for drift"
section.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (this repo's own drift finding motivated the harness).
issue.title: Add installed-copy drift checker script

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md "Factory feedback loop" item 2.

## Task
- repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh and SKILL.md: after the fix pass, every remaining finding becomes
  one bead (title `hygiene: <category>: <short>`, label `hygiene`, priority 3) through the repo's bead
  CLI, chosen from `.needle.yaml` `bead_cli.backend` (`bead` for bead-rs, `bf` otherwise); if the repo
  has no bead store, print the findings and file nothing.
- Dedupe by a `--unique-ref hygiene:<category>:<hash>` so re-runs do not duplicate.
- Never write under `.beads/` directly.

## Acceptance
- Fixture repo with two unfixable findings yields two beads on the first run and zero on the second.
- A repo without `.needle.yaml`/`.beads` yields a printed report and no error.
issue.title: repo-hygiene: file beads for findings it cannot fix, via the repo's declared bead backend

issue.description:
9 skills each carry their own scripts/score-*.sh or scan-*.sh (release-readiness/scripts/scan-release.sh,
repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh, plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh + score-plan.sh,

test-plan-review/scripts/scan-tests.sh, readme-review/scripts/score-readme.sh). Each
independently reimplements: markdown frontmatter parsing, markdown section/header scanning,
and percent/color terminal output formatting.

Add a shared lib/common.sh at repo root with the deduplicated versions of these three
utilities, and refactor the 9 scripts above to source it (`source
"$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh"` or equivalent relative path) instead of reimplementing.
Keep each script's actual scoring logic (the part specific to that skill) untouched — this is
a pure extraction, not a behavior change. Run each refactored script against its existing
sample/fixture input (where one exists, e.g. plan-review's SELF-TEST.md sample) before/after
to confirm output is byte-identical.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list).

issue.close_reason: Completed selective install script for jeds-curated-skills. Created install.sh supporting individual skill installation (--all, --list, or specific names), with non-destructive copies to ~/.claude/skills/ and clear overwrite warnings. Updated README.md to lead with this new installation method.
issue.description:
README.md's install instructions are: clone the whole repo directly into ~/.claude/skills/, or
manually `cp -r <skill> ~/.claude/skills/` one at a time. The first option assumes an empty or
absent ~/.claude/skills/ — on this very machine, ~/.claude/skills/ already has 7 skills from
other sources (bd-to-br-migration, beads-overview, claude-status, find-stubs, gap-review,
generate-image, new-repo) plus 2 already installed from this repo (plan-review, repo-hygiene);
cloning this repo directly over that directory would collide/fail.

Add scripts/install.sh (or root install.sh) supporting:
  ./install.sh <skill-name> [<skill-name>...]   # install just these skills
  ./install.sh --all                             # install every skill in this repo
Both modes copy into ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ without touching any other directory already
there, and print a clear "already installed, overwriting" notice (not a silent clobber) when a
target skill directory already exists. Update README.md's Installation section to lead with
this script instead of the raw `git clone .../.claude/skills` command.

Related: ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md (follow-on work list).
issue.notes:
Created install.sh script with selective installation:
- ./install.sh <skill-name> [<skill-name>...] - installs specific skills
- ./install.sh --all - installs all skills from repo
- ./install.sh --list - lists available skills

Features:
- Copies skills to ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ without touching other directories
- Prints clear 'already installed, overwriting' notice when target exists
- Validates skill names before install
- Returns proper exit codes on failure
- Colored output for clarity

Updated README.md Installation section to lead with script usage.

Tested:
- ./install.sh --list - correctly lists 16 available skills
- ./install.sh plan-author - fresh install worked
- ./install.sh plan-author - reinstall showed warning message

Committed and pushed to main.
issue.title: Add root install.sh for selective, non-destructive skill installs

issue.description:
Implement the static structural-validation harness decided in ADR-1
(docs/plan/plan.md, 'ADR-1: 2026-07-20 — Add a static structural-validation harness for skill
bundles'). Add scripts/validate-skills.sh at repo root that, for every top-level skill
directory (one with a SKILL.md):

1. Frontmatter schema — SKILL.md has a YAML frontmatter block; `name:` matches the directory
   name; `description` and `allowed-tools` are present and non-empty.
2. Reference integrity — every CHECKLIST-*.md / REPORT-TEMPLATE.md / subagents/*.md /
   scripts/*.sh filename mentioned in SKILL.md resolves to a file that actually exists in that
   skill's directory.
3. Shell syntax — every scripts/*.sh passes `bash -n`; if `shellcheck` is on PATH also run it
   and print (don't fail on) warnings — must degrade gracefully when shellcheck is absent
   (it is not installed on this machine as of 2026-07-20).
4. Executable bit — every scripts/*.sh referenced from a SKILL.md invocation snippet is
   `chmod +x`.

Also add scripts/install-hooks.sh that installs scripts/validate-skills.sh as a git
pre-commit hook (hooks aren't versioned by git, so this is the install step for local repo
checkouts).

Exit non-zero and print a clear per-skill report if any check fails. Reference ADR-1 in the
script's header comment.
issue.title: Implement scripts/validate-skills.sh per ADR-1
